subject: How do I calculate encounter rate confidence intervals "by hand"?

messages.author: e53c8e38b16419a5
messages.subject: How do I calculate encounter rate confidence intervals "by hand"?
parts:
Hello,

I am using Distance 6.2 and I am wondering if anybody could please point me towards some references that explain how I can calculate encounter rate confidence intervals.

I get this results screen:


                         Estimate      %CV     df     95% Confidence Interval
                        ------------------------------------------------------
                 n       346.00   
                 k       48.000   
                 L       880.86   
                 n/L    0.39280       13.00    47.00 0.30276      0.50962   
                 Left    0.0000
                 Width   13.340   

and I would like to calculate the confidence intervals on my own (so that I can come up with the results that Distance gives me).


This is my first posting, and I couldn't find any previous threads about how calculate confidence intervals (nor could I find any literature on how to do it), so any help is appreciated.

Thank you,

Brigham Whitman

messages.author: e87c178e8547c106
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] How do I calculate encounter rate confidence intervals "by hand"?
parts:
Hi Brigham,
I'll send you off the list a paper and some slides that explain the
calculations. The reference for others is:

Fewster, R.M., Buckland, S.T., Burnham, K.P., Borchers, D.L., Jupp, P.E.,
Laake, J.L., and Thomas, L. Estimating the encounter rate variance in
distance sampling. Biometrics, 65, 225-236, 2009.

Best wishes,
Rachel Fewster
